title: Wight
html_source:
A wight is a living creature, usually a human being.

You may have learned the term from Tolkien’s LOTR (cf. barrow-wights)

Etymology:
From Middle English wight, wiȝt, from Old English wiht (“wight, person, creature, being, whit, thing, something, anything”), from Proto-Germanic wihtiz (“essence, object”), from Proto-Indo-European wekti- (“cause, sake, thing”), from Proto-Indo-European *wekʷ- (“to say, tell”). Cognate with Scots wicht (“creature, being, human”), Dutch wicht (“child, baby”), German Low German Wicht (“girl; wight”), German Wicht (“wretch, wight, little creature, scoundrel”), Norwegian Bokmål vette (“underground creature, gnome”), Swedish vätte (“underground creature, gnome”), Icelandic vættur (“imp, elf”). See also whit.
